transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. ...Well, I guess I'm here because I just have a hard time sitting still. Like, if I'm stuck in a staff meeting at work, or... maybe a briefing at church. I just get this feeling like there's a motor humming under my skin. I usually end up shifting around a lot. Or I just... find some excuse to stand up and move. That's... pretty much it.
When you're in these situations where you feel that motor humming and need to move around, do you also have trouble focusing on what's being said, or does your mind tend to wander?
Not really. I mean... I hear what they're saying. It's just the sitting still part that gets to me. I don't think my mind wanders much.
When you feel that urge to move around, do you find yourself doing things impulsively without thinking first—like interrupting people, making snap decisions, or acting without planning?

I suppose... sometimes I interrupt. 

Like, if my supervisor is giving me instructions for a job... or maybe one of the church staff. I just... I tend to jump in with what I think they’re going to say before they can finish. 

Sometimes I get it wrong, though. And then they have to correct me. But... yeah, I guess I do that.
When did you first start noticing this feeling of needing to move around and the difficulty sitting still? Was this something that started when you were a child, or is it more recent?

I suppose... it's not a new thing. It goes back to... well, grade school, really. 

I remember getting in trouble back then for... popping out of my seat. And talking over the teacher. Or just... rushing ahead before the directions were finished. 

My mother... she used to say I acted like I was wound too tight. Even as a kid. So... yeah. A long time.

When you feel that motor humming sensation and the urge to move, can you hold completely still if you really try—or does your body shake or tremble even when you're trying your hardest to stay seated?
I don't think I shake. I mean, I don't remember anyone ever telling me I do. I just... I just feel uncomfortable. I don't think my body trembles.
When you're doing something you really enjoy or find interesting—like a hobby or activity you like—do you still feel that same motor humming sensation and need to move around, or does it go away?

I don't really know... I guess it doesn't entirely go away. Even when I'm just trying to relax. 

Like... if my wife and I go fishing, or... if we're sitting through bingo. I still catch myself tapping. Or messing with my tackle box... or the pencil. Sometimes she says I'm talking too loud. It just... gets hard for me to just be quiet and enjoy it. So, yeah. It's still there.
Has anyone ever commented that your hands shake or tremble, or have you noticed visible shaking in your hands or body when you're trying to hold still or do something precise like writing or eating?
No. I haven't noticed anything like that. No one's said anything about shaking.
